en: Regarding the Dharani Method of the Goddess Ratnagarbha:

At that time, Maheśvara, the King of Gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, together with the assembly of goddesses, praised the name of the Heavenly King Ratnagarbha as "Thalakhā. He possesses great majesty, virtue, physical strength, and power.
Thus, one is able to perform extraordinary deeds within the world—
shaking heaven, moving the earth, overturning mountains, and submerging the seas;
victory or defeat in war is achieved through the power of one's resolve.
Wealth, silks, and precious treasures shall accumulate like mountains;
for the enjoyment of the world,
he then spoke this mantra:
Oṃ ṭara khata ra kha vidāre svāhā. If one wishes to receive and uphold this dharma, first paint the form of a celestial maiden (devī).
According to the *mṛttikā-dhāraṇa* rite, [this should be done] seven days prior to the fifth day of the fifth month.
Eat rare congee and observe the long fast;
wherever you intend to go, it must be clean and pure.
When practicing this method, the celestial maidens will come of their own accord without being summoned.
However, one must contemplate and maintain the practice to manifest utmost sincerity.
This rite must be received and maintained on the night of the fifth day of the fifth month; only then will the fruit of accomplishment be realized.
On the night of the fifth day of the fifth month.
Focus your thoughts and maintain mindfulness while reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Do not recite too hurriedly.
When you reach the third watch of the night, your mind will grow weary and resemble sleep.
The heavenly maiden sent her attendants to come and test and toy with them,
strictly forbidding them from speaking with one another.
This occurred for a second time.
The goddess Tārakā came of her own accord to meet him;
however, the practitioner was not permitted to go forth to her.
He then knelt on his right knee, joined his palms, and prostrated twice.
They immediately asked him what he required;
the practitioner answered according to his words,
requesting excellent medicine for longevity and immortality, and for the attainment of spiritual powers.
Regarding the affairs of all things in the world,
he served them throughout his life;
yet the celestial maiden, conceiving desire in her mind, wished to become his wife.
Upon hearing this, the goddess was filled with great joy.
That very night, she granted him all his vows according to his wishes;
if he desired her to be his sister, she became so.
Regarding the ritual matters, one must be clear and distinct, and not harbor any doubts.
As for the method of the mandala, measure two and a half cubits and smear the ground with cow dung mud;
furthermore, coat the ground with fragrant mud.
There should be paintings in five colors, and five-colored silks, each measuring two chi and one cun.
Within the altar, place the seats for the goddesses.
Set out one plate each of ghee, honey, milk, and various fruits.
There are five pieces each of flower-cakes in five colors.
Having mixed chestnuts and wheat with incense flowers, one may make offerings as desired.
As for the method of painting the image, the body of the goddess is two feet and five inches tall.
A flower crown adorns his head, with flowers of exquisite beauty and perfect symmetry.
He wears a purple robe, a golden belt, and black boots;
in his right hand, he holds a lotus flower.
In her left hand she holds a wish-fulfilling jewel (cintāmaṇi).
That goddess is so upright and radiant that no painter in the world could depict her.
One must be skillful and not haggling over prices.
One shall attain spiritual penetration at the appropriate time, with the mind and spirit free and at ease.
Wealth and resources will overflow, and one’s official rank will be promoted to high positions.
He thoroughly understood all calamities and blessings therein;
nobles and commoners, men and women alike, were filled with joy.
Whenever he moved, all the ghosts and spirits came forward to welcome and attend him, honoring him as they would a celestial official.
Upon gazing up with awe and reverence, one immediately attains unimpeded mastery;
even worldly and exquisite arts are accomplished at will. Should anyone come with malicious intent to cause harm, [the practitioner remains unassailable].
He then called out to the bandits, and each of them was able to bind themselves and strike themselves.
He said, "Release [me]! and they were released immediately. It has been verified that those who have fled or died in the world due to worldly calamities are restored;
even the myriad illnesses before one's eyes are all cured by simply directing the mind toward it.
Furthermore, for each of the eight mantras, one must bathe thoroughly and don fresh, clean garments.
One should then recite each mantra twenty-one times before the Buddha and before his image,
after which one may perform the ritual procedure.

First mantra: Oṃ kṣepara tiṭṭha jjaḥ svāhā. Second mantra: Oṃ varatiṭṭha manara svāhā. Third mantra: Oṃ lekhanatiṭṭha ṣṭha svāhā. Fourth mantra: Oṃ pāpalejatiṭṭha svāhā. Fifth mantra: Oṃ vīrajatiṭṭha svāhā. Sixth mantra: Oṃ yakṣa yakṣa tina va svāhā. Seventh mantra: Oṃ cāṭi vicaye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Eighth mantra: Oṃ cālekna yari patiṭṭha svāhā. [Perform the mudrā] by bending the middle and ring fingers.
Press the two thumbnails with the thumbs,
extend the index fingers and little fingers, and place them upon the heart;
hold the rosary with the right hand and recite the mantra.
This is called the Jadelike Ring Seal.
The ritual of the Treasure Store Goddess is completed.
